prompts: We need a landing page, {WS}/landing/index.html in a single file, for the story of Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] `landing/index.html`: a single-file page on Mondrian's *Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow* (1930), using only the facts in `FACTSHEET.md`.

[action]
- The page is itself a Mondrian composition: a CSS grid of white cells split by thick black lines, with a large red block top right, a small blue block bottom left and a small yellow block bottom right.
- The text sits in the white cells. It gives:
  - the painter, with his dates and nationality;
  - the year;
  - the movement (De Stijl, its founding in 1917 and its three Neoplasticism principles);
  - why the work matters;
  - a button to the Wikipedia source from the fact sheet.
- The only external resource is Google Fonts (Jost, with Helvetica/Arial as fallback). Three.js is not used, so the page has no CDN dependency. The red, blue and yellow blocks fade in on load, unless the visitor has reduced-motion set.

Assumptions:
- Three.js was optional, and a flat grid is truer to Mondrian.
- I added no facts, no image of the painting and no dimensions.
- On narrow screens the layout reflows to one or two columns.

[result] Not verified in a browser. I did not open or render the file, and I did not check the console or the font loading. What I did check, by reading the code, is that each of the grid's named areas forms a rectangle, so the layout is valid. The facts match the fact sheet by reading, but I did not diff them line by line.

[next] Open `landing/index.html` in a browser to check the layout visually.
